items.question: How can liberation be claimed if no experience anywhere is devoid of auspicious or inauspicious karma?
premises: auspicious and inauspicious experiences are everywhere
no experience is ever completely devoid of them
liberation requires freedom from such binding experience
items.inference: The verse denies that any experience is free from auspicious or inauspicious content, so liberation cannot rest on mere absence of experience.
uncertainties: whether tena refers to the experiencer or the experience
items.plain_english: Auspicious and inauspicious things are to be experienced, and nowhere is anything devoid of them.

rows.grounds: fused form treated as one token

items.question: Whose mind has become transcendent mind, and what liberation results for that person here?
premises: transcendent mind is the decisive condition
the person whose mind is so transformed is specified
liberation becomes present for that person
items.inference: The verse identifies transcendent mind as the condition under which liberation arises for the qualified person.
uncertainties: whether unmanantu is adverbial or adjectival
items.plain_english: For one whose mind has become transcendent mind, liberation becomes present here.

items.question: Who may attain liberation because sin and merit do not smear that person?
premises: liberation belongs to a specified person
sin and merit do not smear him
items.inference: The verse makes liberation depend on remaining unstained by both sin and merit.
uncertainties: whether pāpapuṇyairna is instrumental or ablative in sense
items.plain_english: Liberation may be his who is not smeared by sin or merit.

items.question: Why is there no doubt about liberation for one compared to a water drop on a lotus leaf?
items.inference: The verse removes doubt by comparing the liberated person to a water drop that does not cling to a lotus leaf.
uncertainties: whether the simile modifies liberation or the person
items.plain_english: There is no doubt about his liberation, like a water drop on a lotus leaf.

items.question: What happens when the body falls and the skull is split, O goddess?
premises: the event occurs at body fall
items.inference: The verse marks skull-splitting at bodily death as the moment for a subsequent transformation.
uncertainties: whether kapālambhidyate is passive or middle
items.plain_english: When the body falls, O goddess, and the skull is split, then...

items.question: What chapter is named as the thirteenth installation emerging in the moon island?
premises: the setting is the moon island
items.inference: The verse identifies the thirteenth chapter as the installation emerging in the moon island.
uncertainties: whether candradvīpa is literal or symbolic
items.plain_english: The thirteenth chapter is the installation emerging in the moon island.

items.question: What is immediately accomplishment-causing and supreme when freed from wheel meditation?
premises: freedom from wheel meditation is stated
the result causes accomplishment and is supreme
items.inference: The verse presents a supreme, immediately effective accomplishment once one is freed from wheel meditation.
uncertainties: whether siddhikaraṃ modifies a hidden noun
items.plain_english: Freed from wheel meditation, it is immediately accomplishment-causing and supreme.

items.question: What wonderful and great wonder-causing thing is the goddess asked to hear?
premises: the object is wonderful and wonder-causing
items.inference: The verse introduces a teaching whose content is both wonderful and productive of wonder.
uncertainties: whether tvamadbhutaṃ is one fused token or two
items.plain_english: Hear, O goddess, this wonderful thing that causes great wonder.

items.question: Which beings and ascetics are enumerated in this list?
items.inference: The verse lists celestial, demonic, and ascetic beings as part of the doctrinal context.
uncertainties: whether garndhavāḥ is a variant spelling
exact role of the list in the argument
items.plain_english: Gandharvas, kinnaras, yakshas, asuras, and ascetics.

items.question: What is the condition of one devoid of kula devotion and deprived of guru devotion?
premises: the condition is stated as a disqualification
items.inference: The verse defines a disqualifying state by the absence of both kula and guru devotion.
uncertainties: whether the locative is absolute or descriptive
items.plain_english: Indeed, one devoid of kula devotion and deprived of guru devotion.

items.question: What qualities characterize deceivers, the miserable, the deluded, and the deficient in truth-reviled contexts?
premises: miserable and deluded persons are named
deficient things occur in truth-reviled contexts
items.inference: The verse groups negative moral and cognitive qualities as marks of unworthy recipients.
uncertainties: whether hīnāni modifies objects or persons
items.plain_english: Deceivers, miserable, deluded, and deficient things in truth-reviled contexts.

items.question: What happens to accomplishment when a teacher gives these disciples to unqualified recipients?
premises: the recipients are specified in context
items.inference: The verse warns that improper transmission of disciples causes loss of accomplishment.
uncertainties: whether ye is subject or relative clause marker
items.plain_english: If a teacher gives these disciples, accomplishment is lost.

items.question: How does one remain devoid of emptiness while engaged in dharma, delight, and anger?
items.inference: The verse links constant engagement in dharma, delight, and anger with being devoid of emptiness.
uncertainties: whether śūnyavarjitaḥ is positive or negative
exact relation among the three locatives
items.plain_english: In dharma and delight, always in anger, one is devoid of emptiness.

items.question: How does one become serene-minded through devotion to gods, fire, discipline, and yoginis?
premises: gods, fire, discipline, and yoginis are objects
items.inference: The verse prescribes devotion to these powers as the path to a serene mind.
uncertainties: whether devāgniyatiyoginyā is dative or genitive in sense
items.plain_english: With devotion to gods, fire, discipline, and yoginis, one is always serene-minded.

items.question: Who should give long life after having well examined and always to him?
items.inference: The verse ties the gift of long life to prior careful examination.
items.plain_english: Having well examined, one should always give long life to him.

items.question: What is the status of one who transgresses guru command in a context hostile to yoginis?
items.inference: The verse identifies transgression of guru command as a serious fault in a hostile yogini context.
uncertainties: whether vidviṣṭe modifies a person or situation
items.plain_english: And in a context hostile to yoginis, a transgressor of guru command.

items.question: To whom should one not give, O goddess, among revilers of Shiva and slanderers of kula Bhairava?
premises: kula Bhairava is the protected figure
items.inference: The verse forbids giving to those who revile Shiva or slander kula Bhairava.
uncertainties: whether na governs dadyāt from context
items.plain_english: Not to a Shiva-reviler, O goddess, nor to a slanderer of kula Bhairava.

items.question: What accumulation is compared to buying an ocean filled with jewels?
premises: an ocean filled with jewels is imagined
items.inference: The verse uses an impossible purchase to emphasize the value or magnitude of accumulation.
uncertainties: whether saṃcayaḥ is wealth or merit
items.plain_english: An accumulation of his is like buying an ocean filled with jewels.

items.question: What determination of all times is this kaula teaching for the great goddess?
premises: it is a determination for all times
items.inference: The verse presents the kaula teaching as a timeless determination.
uncertainties: whether nirṇayam modifies kaulaṃ or a hidden verb
items.plain_english: This kaula teaching, O great goddess, is the determination of all times.

items.question: What best knowledge should be properly given, O goddess, in the sevenfold manner?
items.inference: The verse prescribes proper transmission of best knowledge through a sevenfold process.
items.plain_english: Properly, O goddess, the best knowledge should be given in the sevenfold manner.

items.question: What happens first when one practices the root wheel, O beloved?
items.inference: The verse begins a sequence of effects from practicing the root wheel.
items.plain_english: First, when one practices the root wheel, O beloved.

items.question: What trembling comes first and what shaking follows second?
items.inference: The verse describes a two-stage bodily or energetic response to practice.
uncertainties: whether dhūnanantu is noun or participle
items.plain_english: First trembling comes, then shaking as the second.

items.question: What happens to all mantra and mudra groups when he utters them stammeringly?
premises: all mantra and mudra groups are mentioned
items.inference: The verse indicates that stammering utterance affects the whole group of mantras and mudras.
uncertainties: whether durdurapluta is adverbial or adjectival
items.plain_english: All mantra and mudra groups, indeed, he utters stammeringly.

items.question: What deception of time and transformation of form is addressed to the goddess?
items.inference: The verse pairs temporal deception with transformation of form as doctrinal topics.
uncertainties: whether the two accusatives share one verb
items.plain_english: The deception of time, O goddess, and the transformation of form.
